job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his grandfather sat on their porch in Rajasthan, watching the monsoon clouds gather. 'It is so hot today, Grandpa,' Rohan said, 'does this heat mean the climate is changing?' His grandfather smiled, 'No, Rohan. Weather is what happens outside right now, like today's heat or rain. Climate is the average pattern of weather over many, many years.' He pointed to the fields. 'Some people think global warming is just a future problem, but we see it now through erratic monsoons and intense heatwaves affecting our crops. It is not just about rising temperatures; our rainfall patterns are shifting too. People often blame only big factories for greenhouse gases, but our daily choices, like wasting electricity or using plastic, also add to the problem. Some worry that the greenhouse effect is entirely bad, but it actually keeps Earth warm enough for life. The real danger is the enhanced greenhouse effect, where extra gases trap too much heat. Even if we have a cold winter day, it does not mean the planet is cooling. The long-term trend shows the Earth is steadily warming, causing glaciers to melt and sea levels to rise, partly because warmer water takes up more space than cold water.'

items.evidence: Even if we have a cold winter day, it does not mean the planet is cooling.
items.q: Jaipur has its coldest winter day in years. What does this one day show about global warming?
options: It shows little, since weather differs from climate
It shows the planet has started cooling down
It shows the climate is now a cold one
It shows warming has not really begun yet
items.explain: One cold day is weather, not climate. Grandpa says a cold winter day does not mean the planet is cooling.

wrong.why: thinks a cold day proves global warming is false
thinks climate is just this season's weather
thinks global warming has not started yet

items.evidence: Climate is the average pattern of weather over many, many years.
items.q: Which of these describes Rajasthan's climate rather than its weather?
options: Hot, dry summers year after year for decades
A very hot afternoon on Rohan's porch today
Monsoon clouds gathering over the fields this evening
Heavy rain that fell all through last week
items.explain: Climate is the average weather pattern over many years, so only summers repeated for decades describe climate.

wrong.why: picks today's heat, a nearby detail from the passage
mixes up weather and climate, picking what is happening now
thinks climate is the weather of the present season

items.evidence: Some people think global warming is just a future problem, but we see it now through erratic monsoons and intense heatwaves affecting our crops.
items.q: Why does Grandpa say global warming is not only a problem for later?
options: Because its effects already harm today's crops
Because it will start once glaciers melt
Because every place gets hotter each year
Because one hot day proves it is here
items.explain: Grandpa says we already see it now through erratic monsoons and heatwaves that affect crops.

wrong.why: thinks climate change has not started yet
thinks warming means every place heats up equally each year
thinks one hot day shows the Earth is warming

items.evidence: Some worry that the greenhouse effect is entirely bad, but it actually keeps Earth warm enough for life.
items.q: What would most likely happen if Earth had no greenhouse effect at all?
options: Earth would be too cold for living things
Earth would be safer for all living things
Earth would get more of the Sun's rays
Earth would be hotter from trapped heat
items.explain: The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life, so without it Earth would be too cold.

wrong.why: thinks the greenhouse effect is always harmful
thinks greenhouse gases block the Sun's rays
reverses cause and effect about trapping heat

items.evidence: People often blame only big factories for greenhouse gases, but our daily choices, like wasting electricity or using plastic, also add to the problem.
items.q: Meena leaves the fan and lights on in an empty room. How does this affect climate change?
options: It adds to greenhouse gases through wasted electricity
It adds nothing, as only factories make such gases
It adds nothing, as these gases are too tiny
It adds poison gas to the air in the room
items.explain: Grandpa says daily choices like wasting electricity also add greenhouse gases, not only big factories.

wrong.why: thinks only factories and cars add greenhouse gases
thinks small amounts of gases do not matter
thinks carbon dioxide harms by being poisonous to breathe
